title: The Messengership Of Prophet Muhammad 16th Degree 2nd Proof The Quran As Decree And Its Miraculousness

questions.question: What is the main claim made about the person described in this passage?
questions.answer: He is presented as completely truthful and incapable of lying because of his relation to the divine message he delivers.

questions.question: What does the “decree” in his hand refer to?
questions.answer: It refers to the Qur’an.

questions.question: Who is said to have accepted and affirmed this decree across the centuries?
questions.answer: More than three hundred million people in every century.

questions.question: How many kinds of wonder are mentioned for this decree?
questions.answer: Seven.

questions.question: Besides those seven kinds, what other measure of the Qur’an’s extraordinary nature is mentioned?
questions.answer: It is said to have forty aspects of miraculousness.

questions.question: What two major points are said to have been proven elsewhere with strong evidence?
questions.answer: The Qur’an’s miraculous nature and that it is the speech of the Creator.

questions.question: How is the other treatise described in order to show its importance?
questions.answer: It is described as a famous work and compared to the sun within the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: According to the traveller’s conclusion, why is lying impossible for the one who conveys this decree?
questions.answer: Because lying would mean betraying both the message and the One who sent it.

questions.question: In this passage, what object is used as a major proof for the truthfulness of the messenger?
questions.answer: The Qur’an is used as a major proof.

questions.question: How is the source of the Qur’an described?
questions.answer: It is described as coming from the Creator of all beings.

questions.question: What does the phrase about every century imply about the decree’s influence?
questions.answer: It implies that its influence is continuous and not limited to one era.

questions.question: Why would lying by the messenger count as a violation of the decree itself?
questions.answer: Because his role is to faithfully deliver and announce it, so dishonesty would go against the message he carries.

questions.question: Why would such lying also count as betrayal toward the One who issued the decree?
questions.answer: Because the decree belongs to Allah, so falsehood in delivering it would break the trust owed to Him.

questions.question: What is the effect of mentioning both the message and the Sender in the final sentence?
questions.answer: It strengthens the argument by showing that lying would be wrong on both levels.

questions.question: What is the central focus of this short section: the law, miracles, community history, or the divine book?
questions.answer: The central focus is the divine book.

questions.question: What name is given to that divine book in the passage?
questions.answer: It is called the Qur’an of Mighty Stature.

questions.question: How many broad ways of wonder are mentioned for the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Seven broad ways are mentioned.

questions.question: How many aspects of miraculousness are said to belong to it?
questions.answer: Forty.

questions.question: What two descriptions are given of the person connected to this decree?
questions.answer: He is described as the one who carries it and the one who announces it.

questions.question: What does the passage say has already been done in another work regarding the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Its miraculousness and divine origin have already been explained there with solid proofs.

questions.question: Why does this passage not repeat all those proofs?
questions.answer: Because it points readers to that fuller discussion and keeps this section concise.

questions.question: What does the continued affirmation of the decree by hundreds of millions indicate about its reception?
questions.answer: It indicates deep and lasting acceptance among people over time.

questions.question: What moral failure would lying involve according to the passage?
questions.answer: It would involve unfaithfulness to the revelation and disloyalty to Allah.

questions.question: What final judgment does the traveller make about the messenger’s honesty?
questions.answer: He judges that falsehood is impossible for him.

questions.question: What is being “held” in the passage, and what does that image suggest?
questions.answer: A decree is being held, and the image suggests responsibility, authority, and entrusted duty.

questions.question: Who is described as the lord of the universe in this passage?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: Why is the decree important in the argument about the messenger?
questions.answer: Because the greatness and divine source of the decree support the trustworthiness of the one delivering it.

questions.question: What role does the long history of affirmation play in this reasoning?
questions.answer: It serves as support that the decree has enduring recognition and weight.

questions.question: How does the passage combine quantity and quality in speaking about the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It mentions both the vast number of its followers and the many forms of its miraculousness.

questions.question: Why is treachery especially serious in this case?
questions.answer: Because the trust is not merely human; it concerns a message issued by Allah.

questions.question: What kind of certainty does the traveller express at the end: doubt, probability, or impossibility?
questions.answer: He expresses impossibility.

questions.question: How does the passage use reference to another book without weakening its own point?
questions.answer: It borrows the weight of detailed proof from that book while making a brief clear conclusion here.

questions.question: What does this section teach about the ethics of carrying revelation?
questions.answer: Carrying revelation requires complete honesty and faithfulness.

questions.question: If the messenger were dishonest, what two trusts would be broken according to the passage?
questions.answer: The trust of the revealed decree and the trust owed to its Sender.

questions.question: Give a brief summary of the argument in this paragraph.
questions.answer: The Qur’an is presented as a divine and miraculous decree affirmed across generations, so the one entrusted to convey it cannot be a liar.

questions.question: What is the purpose of mentioning a detailed treatise on the Qur’an’s miraculousness?
questions.answer: The purpose is to show that the claim is supported elsewhere by extensive evidence.

questions.question: What picture of the Qur’an emerges from this passage?
questions.answer: It appears as a majestic divine message with many signs of wonder and a vast history of acceptance.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention both seven wonders and forty miraculous aspects?
questions.answer: To show that its extraordinary nature is rich and multi-layered.

questions.question: What can a reader infer about the seriousness of the messenger’s mission?
questions.answer: It is a mission of the highest seriousness because he carries revelation from Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage connect public proclamation with personal honesty?
questions.answer: It suggests that openly declaring a divine decree requires complete truthfulness.

questions.question: What consequence would lying have for the messenger’s relationship to the decree?
questions.answer: It would mean failing his duty toward it.

questions.question: What consequence would lying have for his relationship to Allah?
questions.answer: It would mean betrayal of the trust given by Allah.

questions.question: What does the phrase about acceptance in every century add beyond a single historical moment?
questions.answer: It shows permanence and continuity across time.

questions.question: In this passage, what supports the claim that the messenger does not lie: only his personal character, or also the nature of the book he brings?
questions.answer: Also the nature of the book he brings.

questions.question: What is the strongest concluding point of the paragraph?
questions.answer: A messenger entrusted with Allah’s decree cannot be deceitful without contradicting his whole mission.

questions.question: What single piece of evidence is highlighted in this section as proof for the messenger’s truthfulness?
questions.answer: The evidence highlighted is the Qur’an as the divine decree he carries.

questions.question: How is the scale of the Qur’an’s acceptance described?
questions.answer: It is described as being affirmed by more than three hundred million people in each century.

questions.question: What does that repeated acceptance across centuries imply about the decree’s place among people?
questions.answer: It implies that it has lasting authority and influence.

questions.question: What two features of the Qur’an are especially stressed here?
questions.answer: Its miraculous nature and its being the word of the Creator.

questions.question: What is the effect of saying the Qur’an is wondrous in seven ways?
questions.answer: It emphasizes that its excellence appears from multiple angles.

questions.question: What is added by saying it has forty aspects of miraculousness?
questions.answer: It adds detail and breadth to the claim of its extraordinary nature.

questions.question: Why does the passage move quickly past the detailed proofs?
questions.answer: Because those detailed proofs are said to be available in a separate well-known work.

questions.question: What does this quick move allow the passage to focus on instead?
questions.answer: It allows the passage to focus on what the Qur’an implies about the honesty of its messenger.

questions.question: According to the traveller, what would lying by the messenger amount to in ethical terms?
questions.answer: It would amount to disloyalty and breach of trust.

questions.question: Why is falsehood presented as impossible rather than merely unlikely?
questions.answer: Because it would directly conflict with his role as faithful bearer and announcer of Allah’s decree.

questions.question: Write the argument of the passage as a short cause-and-effect statement.
questions.answer: Since he faithfully carries and proclaims a divine, miraculous book accepted across ages, deceit cannot belong to him.
